focus: Adversarial safety audit of P1-P7 contracts using counterexamples and negative controls for authority leakage, non-convergent settlement, stale fences, dual-head cuts, supersession/nogood races, refusal misuse, and human-gate invalidation
noveltyJustification: Prior iterations specified each contract and the P3 schedule model; this audit adds seven compositional counterexamples, exposes a silent fixed-point-cap failure, defines a consistency-closed dual-ledger cut, requires one serializable truth-admission conflict domain, and closes the post-authorization human-context invalidation window.
keyFindings: Verified projections remain advisory until an explicit selected-authority state and epoch guard converts them for control use
Belief settlement must prove quiescence and fail closed on cycles oscillation repeated state or bound exhaustion
Stale claimant work is rejected only by atomic per-resource fence and expected-version validation at the protected mutation
Domain and authorization heads form a reference-closed cut rather than equal sequences or a synthetic total order
All truth-affecting supersession and nogood candidates require one serializable admission head or equivalent conflict-key transaction
TransitionRefusalV1 is an authority-zero non-command whose advice always requires a fresh authorized request
Human gate append must atomically revalidate gate fence/version and the declared semantic dependency vector after allow

ruledOut.approach: Use the freshest replay-verified projection as control authority
ruledOut.reason: Freshness and verification do not select the governed authority owner or epoch

ruledOut.approach: Treat a deterministic round cap as fixed-point convergence
ruledOut.reason: The reducer can exit with pending changes and publish a parity-dependent non-fixed state

ruledOut.approach: Check a claim fence only before the protected mutation
ruledOut.reason: A successor can take over between validation and commit

ruledOut.approach: Require equal domain and audit heads or read each latest independently
ruledOut.reason: Valid denial-only cuts have audit lead while domain events require their referenced allow inside the audit cut

ruledOut.approach: Serialize supersession and nogood changes only by direct relation key
ruledOut.reason: Their transitive truth closures can overlap even when direct IDs differ

ruledOut.approach: Auto-apply a refusal suggestion after transport success
ruledOut.reason: A suggestion contains no current proof fence capability or effect authority

ruledOut.approach: Validate human gate context only when minting the allow
ruledOut.reason: A load-bearing dependency can invalidate after authorization but before edge append

nextFocus: Concrete versioned schemas, implementation seams, and staged adoption order
